issues.title: Drop unregistered providers from CUDA diffusion IR op defaults
issues.body:
CudaOmniPlatform.get_default_ir_op_priority() unconditionally prioritizes the vllm_c provider for rms_norm/fused_add_rms_norm. The vllm_c IR kernels are only registered on newer GPU architectures; on sm70 (e.g. Tesla V100) they are absent, so IrOp._filter_priority_impls asserts and crashes diffusion worker startup:

  AssertionError: All providers in priority must be registered implementations.

Fix: filter each priority list against the providers actually registered for that op (after current_platform.import_ir_kernels(), mirroring IrOpPriorityConfig._iter_op_priorities), falling back to native only. On devices where vllm_c is registered the priorities are unchanged.

Tests now derive expectations from the real registry instead of hardcoded lists, and a new regression test hides vllm_c from the registry to reproduce an sm70-like registry on any device.

Validated end-to-end on 2x Tesla V100 (sm70) with Qwen-Image-2.1 TP=2.

## Test Plan
**vLLM Version:** vLLM 0.30.1.dev0 (commit ced6857af)

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** based on latest main (a3d7a0444); originally developed and validated against d9bb1c915 (0.30.0-era deployment on the test machine)

 - Hardware: 2x Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB (sm70), CUDA 12.6
 - pytest tests/platforms/test_cuda_ir_op_priority.py -v on a CUDA machine: registry-derived expectations, the #4964 inductor regression, an sm70-like registry simulated by hiding vllm_c (hardware-independent), and the unknown-op fallback unit test (new, addresses review P3)
- e2e: serve a diffusion model on 2x Tesla V100  (sm70) and run a generation request

## Test Result
- 8/8 unit tests pass on real sm70 hardware
- e2e on 2x V100 (Qwen-Image-2.1, TP=2, --dtype float16): server starts, generation returns HTTP 200 (~10 s/image)

issues.title: [Bugfix][Diffusion] Gate attention-mask capability flags per platform (fixes XPU noise)
issues.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
FIX #6882

## Purpose

`HiDream-ai/HiDream-O1-Image` generates **pure noise** on XPU — exit 0, no warning. `supports_piecewise_spans` was a plain class attribute: `False` on the `AttentionBackend` base, but hardcoded `True` on all three flash backends (`flash_attn.py:175`, `flash_attn_hub.py:85`/`:253`) regardless of platform — and `FLASH_ATTN` is what HiDream-O1 selects on XPU. Only `forward_cuda` dispatches `piecewise_attn` over `AttentionMetadata.full_attn_spans`. `hidream_o1_image_transformer.py` trusted the flag, skipped building the equivalent `attn_mask`, and XPU/NPU then ran **fully dense unmasked attention** — text rows that must stay causal attended to future image tokens. Full analysis in #6882.

A flag describes the `forward_*` that actually runs, not the backend class, so the mask-capability flags become platform-gated `classmethod`s. CUDA / ROCm / MUSA flag values are identical before and after.

- `abstract.py` — `supports_piecewise_spans()` becomes a `classmethod` defaulting to `False`; new `supports_dense_attention_mask()` defaults to `supports_attention_mask()`, which only promises *some* mask is read (several kernels take just a 2D `[B, Skv]` padding mask).
- `flash_attn.py`, `flash_attn_hub.py` — in all three backends spans are `True` only for the CUDA family, exactly the set that reaches `forward_cuda` (ROCm/MUSA via base-class `forward_hip` / `forward_musa` delegation). The hub backends are converted along with the plain one because the base declaration is now a `classmethod`: leaving their `supports_piecewise_spans: bool = True` in place would shadow it with a non-callable and break every caller.
- `cudnn_attn.py`, `vdnh3_attn.py` — the same conversion for two flag declarations that landed on main after this PR was opened (`CUDNN_ATTN`'s via #8099, the new `VDNH3_ATTN` backend via #8439). Both are CUDA-only and keep their old values (`True` / `False`); left as `bool` attributes, every `supports_piecewise_spans()` call on them raised `TypeError: 'bool' object is not callable`.
- `flash_attn.py` — only this backend overrides `supports_dense_attention_mask()`, returning `False` on XPU alone, where its one mask route is `_forward_varlen_masked`, which asserts 2D. The two hub backends inherit the `abstract.py` default and keep reporting `True`.
- `layer.py` — `_run_local_attention` reroutes a >2D mask to the existing `sdpa_fallback` with a `warning_once`, scoped to backends that *claim* mask support so it cannot preempt `TRTLLM_ATTN`'s deliberate `ValueError`. `_assert_piecewise_compatible` now calls the flag.
- `hidream_o1_image_transformer.py` — HiDream-O1's probe now calls the flag. This `()` is what turns the noise into an image.
- `qwen_image_21_transformer.py` — the other model-side consumer, from the same #8099, gets the same `()`. Without it the bound method is always truthy, so `attn_path_hint="auto"` picked `"piecewise"` for every backend — including `TORCH_SDPA`, which then hit the `_assert_piecewise_compatible` `ValueError`.

| Platform | `supports_piecewise_spans()` | Mask reroute | Net effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA / ROCm / MUSA | `True` (was `True`) | no | **No change** |
| XPU | `False` (was `True`) | yes | **Fixed** — model builds the mask, layer runs it on SDPA; verified e2e |
| NPU | `False` (was `True`) | no | **Unverified** — a 4D mask now reaches `aclnnFlashAttentionScore` instead of being skipped, which should be a strict improvement over the dense unmasked run, but no NPU hardware was available. Needs confirmation from someone who has one; see the follow-up on `mindiesd` mask conventions below before assuming it is fixed. |

The reroute fires for exactly one backend on one platform: `FLASH_ATTN` on XPU. It needs `supports_attention_mask()` *and* `not supports_dense_attention_mask()`, and `flash_attn.py` is the only backend that overrides the latter — every other backend inherits the `abstract.py` default, where the two are the same value, so the pair can never both hold. `CUDNN_ATTN`, `FLASHINFER_ATTN`, `TORCH_SDPA` and the two hub backends cannot reroute.

### Scope

Per review, this PR is only the XPU correctness fix: `abstract.py` + the backend flags + `layer.py` + the two model-side `()` fixes. Unrelated fixes that were riding along have been reverted out; the one still open is listed under Follow-ups.

### Reviewer attention

- **The reroute is not HiDream-only.** On XPU, every model that hands `FLASH_ATTN` a >2D mask now runs that layer on SDPA after one `warning_once` — HunyuanImage3, glm_image, flux, flux2 and ernie_image all unsqueeze to 4D before `Attention`. Previously those masks hit `forward_xpu`'s 2D assert, so this turns a hard failure into a working run. CUDA keeps HunyuanImage3's 4D mask + spans on `piecewise_attn`.
- **`supports_dense_attention_mask()` is deliberately `True` on CUDA**, though only *conditionally* honored there: `forward_cuda` honors a >2D mask only via `piecewise_attn`, so a >2D mask *without* spans still hits the 2D assert — reachable by `lingbot_video` and `glm_image`. Returning `False` fixes both but drags HunyuanImage3 (4D mask *with* spans) off `piecewise_attn` onto SDPA, so it is a follow-up. Same for the hub backends.
- **`build_hidream_o1_attention_mask` is newly load-bearing on XPU/NPU.** It was dead code there before this PR, so its test file is new coverage for existing unexercised code rather than for anything this PR rewrites; the function itself is untouched.
- **The 4D additive bf16 mask never reaches `forward_xpu`.** `layer.py` diverts it to SDPA first, so the reverted `torch.any(~attention_mask)` on that path is not on the HiDream-O1 route. Were it ever reached with an additive mask it would raise on `~` over bf16 rather than fail silently.
- **mypy does not catch the `bool`-shadows-`classmethod` regression**, which is how `CUDNN_ATTN` / `VDNH3_ATTN` slipped through the merge. The registry-wide test below is the guard.

## Test Plan

136 new cases: 134 CPU (`core_model`), 2 hardware-gated.

- `test_mask_capability_flags.py` (new, 116)
  - The platform table above asserted rather than described: both flags × three flash backends × five platforms, through a real `OmniPlatform` subclass.
  - The `forward_hip` / `forward_musa` → `forward_cuda` delegation the ROCm/MUSA `True` rests on, and that the flags are callables rather than truthy attributes.
  - The `_mask_needs_sdpa` truth table over 2D/3D/4D masks × mask-aware / dense-capable / mask-blind backends.
  - `_run_local_attention` dispatch with `FLASH_ATTN` on a patched platform, recording which impl actually runs: XPU sends 4D (with or without spans) and 3D masks to `sdpa_fallback` and keeps 2D / no mask on flash; CUDA keeps HunyuanImage3's 4D mask + spans on flash; NPU keeps 4D on flash.
  - Every backend in `DiffusionAttentionBackendEnum` × five platforms answers both flags as a callable returning `bool`, so a future `supports_piecewise_spans: bool = ...` fails CI. Backends that cannot be imported on the host are skipped (`SAGE_ATTN_3` on XPU).
- `test_hidream_o1_attention_mask.py` (new, 18) — rows causal or full at `seq_len` 129 / 1000 / 4231 across bf16 / fp16 / fp32 against an independent `torch.where` reference, asserting the fully-unmasked row *count* and not just the values, since a partially-applied mask writes correct values into the rows it reaches and silently leaves the rest causal. Also `HiDreamO1ImageTransformer.supports_piecewise_attention` over stub backends (all on / all off / mixed), which is the property the pipeline reads to decide whether to build the mask. The 2 `hardware_test` cases build the mask on the accelerator itself and skip rather than false-pass when none is visible; both ran on XPU here.
- `test_attn_path_probe.py` (new, 2) — Qwen-Image-2.1's `_resolve_attn_path("auto")` returns `"piecewise"` / `"mask"` according to the backend's `supports_piecewise_spans()`.
- `test_attention_config.py` — no new cases, only the stubs the flag change invalidates: three `SimpleNamespace` backends whose `supports_piecewise_spans` becomes a callable, a `_mask_needs_sdpa` stub for the one test that drives `_run_local_attention` directly, and a `FlashAttentionBackend` subclass with both flags pinned to the CUDA-family answers so those CPU dispatch assertions do not depend on the host platform.

Each new guard was checked against its regression: dropping the `()` in either model probe, reverting `CUDNN_ATTN` / `VDNH3_ATTN` to `bool` attributes, or disabling the reroute in `layer.py` each fails the corresponding tests. Across `tests/diffusion/attention/`, `tests/diffusion/models/hidream_o1_image/` and `tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/` on XPU, the failing set is identical to a clean `main` worktree on the same container (54 pre-existing environment failures, none new).

**vLLM Version:** 0.32.0 (torch 2.14.0+xpu)

## Test Result

HiDream-O1-Image, 2048x2048, `--seed 42`, on Intel Graphics [0xe223], 30.3 GiB each. `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1` is required on this box for an unrelated Triton/Intel defect. Timings exclude a discarded warm-up generation (first-run kernel JIT).

| TP | Steps | Generate (s) | Peak memory* | Before this PR | After |
|----|-------|--------------|--------------|----------------|-------|
| 1x | 8 | 14.9 | 15.2 GiB | **noise** ❌ | coherent image, legible sign text ✅ |
| 2x | 8 | 9.4 | 8.3 GiB/card | **noise** ❌ | coherent image, legible sign text ✅ |
| 2x | 50 | 57.4 | 8.4 GiB/card | **noise** ❌ | coherent image, legible sign text ✅ |

\* Peak memory from the earlier run on vLLM 0.29.0 / torch 2.13.0; not re-measured on 0.32.0.

"Before" is `main` at the merge base, same script and seed, re-run on 0.32.0 for all three rows: SSIM vs the baseline is 0.053 (TP1/8), 0.029 (TP2/8) and 0.032 (TP2/50), against 0.49 / 0.47 / 0.82 after.

The reroute is observable in the log — `layer.py:776` emits `Attention backend 'FLASH_ATTN' cannot honor a 4D attn_mask on this platform; running this layer on SDPA` once per run.

At 50 steps against the CUDA-generated `tests/assets/hidream_o1/hidream_o1_baseline.png`, using the same LANCZOS downscale the accuracy test applies: SSIM **0.8174** (passes the 0.8 gate), PSNR **18.577** (just under the CUDA-tuned 19.0), visually indistinguishable. `FLASH_ATTN` and an explicit `DIFFUSION_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TORCH_SDPA` are **bit-identical** (max abs diff 0 over the full 2048x2048 RGB image), which is what the reroute guarantees, so the PSNR gap is XPU-vs-CUDA numerics rather than a masking difference. These numbers reproduce exactly on both the 0.29.0 and 0.32.0 stacks.

- Not covered: no CUDA or NPU hardware, so the CUDA/ROCm/MUSA "no change" claim rests on the flag values being identical before and after rather than on an e2e run, and the NPU row of the table above is explicitly unverified. The same applies to `CUDNN_ATTN`, `VDNH3_ATTN` and Qwen-Image-2.1: their behavior is restored to what `main` had, verified on CPU only.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

Split out of this PR at review request — an independent fix to a pre-existing bug, not needed for the XPU noise fix:

- **`torch.any(~attention_mask)` mis-routes int keep-masks** at four flash call sites (`forward_cuda` / `forward_xpu` in `flash_attn.py`, and both hub backends): `~1 == -2`, so every int keep-mask is unconditionally treated as padded and takes the slower masked-varlen path. Qwen-Image is the affected in-tree model. The same helper should reject an additive float mask instead of inverting its meaning inside `_unpad_input`.

Pre-existing and untouched by this PR:

- **`lingbot_video` and `glm_image` cannot use `FLASH_ATTN` on CUDA** with a >2D mask and no spans. Make the reroute predicate metadata-aware: reroute unless spans are present *and* `supports_piecewise_spans()`. Needs CUDA hardware, since it changes which kernel HunyuanImage3 runs on.
- **HiDream-O1 on NPU** now builds an additive bf16 `[1,1,S,S]` mask that `forward_fa_npu` passes unchanged into `mindiesd.attention_forward`, where every other producer supplies a bool keep-mask — so if `mindiesd` reads it as one the semantics invert. This is why the NPU row above is marked unverified rather than fixed. That path ran dense and silently wrong before this PR too.
- `SAGE_ATTN`, `SAGE_ATTN_3` and `RAINFUSION_ATTN` silently ignore an `attn_mask` instead of raising; they should either raise like `TRTLLM_ATTN` or opt into the reroute. And the CUDA-tuned PSNR threshold in `tests/e2e/accuracy/test_hidream_o1_image.py` needs a per-platform value before that test can gate XPU.

**BEFORE SUBMITTING:** read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and run the [precheck-pr skill](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/main/.claude/skills/precheck-pr/SKILL.md) with the code agent for a self-check against project conventions.

issues.title: [Bugfix][Diffusion] Evaluate dense 4D attention masks on SDPA instead of the 2D-only flash path
issues.body:
## Contributor intent (required human answers)

### 1. What outcome do you want to achieve?

Make the Qwen-Image-2.1 CI lanes and multi-request serving work when a batch is padded or heterogeneous, instead of failing every such request with `AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)` (#9187, #9111, #8830).

### 2. What is the highest-leverage variable for that outcome?

Which backend evaluates the dense 4D block-causal mask that the model builds for padded/heterogeneous batches. FlashAttention's masked varlen path only accepts a 2D key-padding mask, so the choice of path — not the mask content — decides whether the request succeeds.

### 3. How will this work move that variable?

It makes the backend capability explicit (`supports_dense_pair_mask`), and when the selected backend cannot consume a 4D mask the Attention layer evaluates that call with SDPA, which handles the pair mask exactly. Piecewise-span metadata is untouched, so the unpadded homogeneous path keeps using FlashAttention.

### 4. Whose customer or user needs does this address, and what are those needs?

Users serving Qwen-Image-2.1 (and any diffusion model that emits a dense pair mask) with more than one prompt, and the CI owners of the Diffusion X2I/X2T perf lanes. They need a batch with mixed prompt lengths to produce an image rather than an HTTP 500, and they need the nightly perf guard to be green.

## Purpose

Before: `supports_attention_mask()` returns True for the whole FlashAttention backend, but `FlashAttentionImpl._forward_varlen_masked` asserts `attention_mask.ndim == 2`. Qwen-Image-2.1 documents two attention representations — piecewise `full_attn_spans` for homogeneous, unpadded batches, and a dense `(batch, 1, q, kv)` block-causal `attn_mask` otherwise — so any padded or heterogeneous batch reached the masked-varlen path with a 4D tensor and died inside the kernel. On A100 that is the reported perf-lane failure; on L20 it is an HTTP 500 for mixed prompt lengths (#9111); with `--max-num-seqs 8` it is the same crash (#8830).

After: backends declare whether they can consume a dense pair mask (`supports_dense_pair_mask`, default False). SDPA, cuDNN and FlashInfer set it True — SDPA evaluates arbitrary boolean pair masks natively, cuDNN FMHA consumes the mask through torch SDPA (verified against the SDPA reference on the same geometry), and FlashInfer's `_pack_mask_for_flashinfer` already collapses the head dim and broadcasts a 4D mask into its `custom_mask`. When a 4D mask arrives without piecewise spans and the selected backend does not support it, the Attention layer routes the call to its existing SDPA fallback and logs one warning. Piecewise metadata is unaffected: the spans carry the structure there, so FlashAttention keeps running that path. An explicitly selected backend still raises `NotImplementedError` with an actionable message rather than silently switching, matching the existing cross-attention fallback contract.

The kernel assert stays as a guard for direct backend use, so the capability claim and the implementation can no longer drift silently.

User guide/example unchanged: no CLI surface, no config key, no model behavior change. The masked result is identical to what SDPA computes for the same mask (the tests compare against SDPA on the same geometry).

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.31.0 (test host) / 0.32.0 (CI)

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** `15bce3458`

- `pytest tests/diffusion/attention/ tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/ -q --ignore=tests/diffusion/attention/test_ring_vllm_flash_attn.py` on an A100-80GB host
- New tests in `tests/diffusion/attention/test_flash_attn.py`:
  - capability flags (`FLASH_ATTN` False; `SDPA`, `CUDNN_ATTN`, `FLASHINFER_ATTN` True)
  - block-causal mask reproducer: the flash kernel still rejects the 4D mask; the `Attention` layer returns the SDPA result with the flash backend never called
  - the same 4D mask **with** `full_attn_spans` still runs on the flash backend and matches the SDPA reference
- Reproducer geometry matches the model: right-padded text prefix (3/40 valid) + two image blocks of 8 tokens, mask `(q >= k) | same_block` minus padded keys.

## Test Result
### End-to-end (A100-80GB, real model, real server)

Qwen-Image-2.1 served with `vllm serve --omni --max-num-seqs 4`, four concurrent requests with **different prompt lengths** (the batch is padded to the longest prompt, which is what makes the model build the 4D block-causal mask). Identical commands before and after the change, only the patch stashed/unstashed.

**Before (unpatched)** — 3 of 4 requests return 500, the mixed-length wave dies inside the kernel:

```
req2 http=200 t=1.96s
req1 http=500 t=5.04s
req3 http=500 t=5.04s
req4 http=500 t=5.04s
{"error":{"message":"Image generation failed: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)",
 "type":"Internal Server Error","param":null,"code":500}}
$ grep -c "attention_mask must be 2D" serve_before.log
24
```

**After (this PR)** — all four return 200 and the fallback is recorded exactly once:

```
req1 http=200 t=19.14s     req2 http=200 t=22.52s
req3 http=200 t=19.15s     req4 http=200 t=22.53s
$ grep -c "Using SDPA for a dense 4D attention mask" serve_batch.log
1
$ grep -c "attention_mask must be 2D" serve_batch.log
0
```

Single-request (batch=1) traffic is unaffected: with no cross-request padding the model keeps using the piecewise-span flash path and no fallback warning is emitted, which is why the earlier single-prompt run stayed on flash.

(The requests are served sequentially in waves of up to 4, so a request that happens to share a wave with same-length prompts — `req2` above — survives even unpatched; the failure needs a mixed-length wave, which is what the CI high-concurrency lane produces.)

Before the change, the reproducer on A100-80GB fails at both levels:

```
[flash] REPRODUCED: AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)
[sdpa] reference OK (1, 1536, 24, 64)
[layer] selected backend: FLASH_ATTN
[layer] REPRODUCED: AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)
```

After the change:

```
Using SDPA for a dense 4D attention mask because FLASH_ATTN only supports a 2D key-padding mask.
[flash] REPRODUCED: AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)   # kernel guard intact
[sdpa] reference OK (1, 1536, 24, 64)
[layer] OK (1, 1536, 24, 64) max_abs_diff_vs_sdpa=0.0000
```

Full suite:

```
1199 passed, 216 skipped, 25 warnings
```

(The two `test_trtllm_contract` failures in the raw run are pre-existing on this host — TensorRT-LLM is not installed in the test environment; they fail identically without this change. `test_ring_vllm_flash_attn.py` cannot be collected against vLLM 0.31 because it imports `RequestError` from `vllm.outputs`, also unrelated.)

## Related

Fixes #9187
Fixes #9111
Fixes #8830

issues.title: [Bugfix] Flash attention: fall back to SDPA for 4D block-causal masks (#8830)
issues.body:
## Contributor intent

1. **What outcome do you want to achieve?** Fix issue #8830 so Qwen-Image-2.1 completes text-to-image generation with the FlashAttention diffusion backend on heterogeneous/padded batches instead of asserting.
2. **What is the highest-leverage variable?** The flash backend's acceptance of the 4D block-causal mask — the exact crash site. A targeted dispatch change there fixes every request on such batches without touching the model layer.
3. **How will this work move that variable?** `FlashAttentionImpl.forward_cuda` already has a masked path; non-2D masks now route to a SDPA fallback, which consumes arbitrary 4D masks natively and preserves the block-causal semantics.
4. **Whose customer or user needs does this address?** Users serving Qwen-Image-2.1 with the flash backend and `--max-num-seqs > 1` / heterogeneous image sizes — their requests crash with `AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D`.

## Purpose

**What broke.** On a padded/heterogeneous batch, `QwenImage21Transformer` builds a dense 4D block-causal mask `(batch, 1, seq_q, seq_k)` via `_build_block_causal_mask`. The FlashAttention backend's `_forward_varlen_masked` only accepts a 2D key-padding mask and asserts `attention_mask.ndim == 2`, crashing every request.

**Root cause.** The FA varlen path (`_unpad_input`/`_upad_input`) filters query and key with the same per-key 2D mask, which cannot express block-causal structure. The 4D mask is produced exactly when padding is present (`has_padding or sp_padding -> "mask"` path in `_resolve_attn_path`), so single-request serving that never forms a padded batch is unaffected.

**Fix.** In `vllm_omni/diffusion/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`, `forward_cuda` now dispatches non-2D attention masks to a new `_forward_4d_masked_sdpa` (SDPA), which consumes 4D masks directly and preserves block-causal semantics. 2D key-padding masks keep the existing varlen path; the change is confined to the flash backend and does not touch the model layer.

**Repro.** Serve Qwen-Image-2.1 with flash attention and a padded batch:
```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 --omni --step-execution --max-num-seqs 2
# then send two concurrent /v1/chat/completions with different image sizes
```
Each request asserts `attention_mask must be 2D` before this fix and completes after it. The regression test reproduces the 4D-mask dispatch at the unit level.

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.31.0
**vLLM-Omni Commit:** 2806b030d

- CPU regression tests (new file `tests/diffusion/attention/test_flash_4d_mask_fallback.py`): `7 passed`. Covers fallback numerics vs exact masked-matmul reference, key-padding variant, the `forward_cuda` 4D->SDPA dispatch guard, and 2D masks staying on the varlen path.
- A100 (A100-PCIE-40GB, torch 2.13.0+cu129): the real `_build_block_causal_mask` -> real `FlashAttentionImpl.forward_cuda` with a 4D mask routes to SDPA and matches reference (`max|out-ref| ≈ 1e-6` fp32); the pre-fix varlen path asserts on the same mask; `_resolve_attn_path` routing (`has_padding -> "mask"`) confirmed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.

## Test Result

Before this fix the 4D-mask path asserts; after it, the masked forward returns correct output (CPU unit + A100 numeric check above).

issues.title: [Hardware][Ascend] Fuse Qwen-Image-2.1 QKV norm and RoPE
issues.body:
## Contributor intent (required human answers)

### 1. What outcome do you want to achieve?

Bring the existing Qwen-Image-2.1 Norm/RoPE optimization onto current main, address the review feedback, and integrate the public MindIE-SD interface through the existing shared fusion layer.

### 2. What is the highest-leverage variable for that outcome?

The QKV preprocessing boundary: reuse the fused operator while keeping model-specific rotary positions and cache/attention ownership in the model. The original performance motivation is tracked in [#8774](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8774).

### 3. How will this work move that variable?

Extend `layers/fused_qk_norm_rope.py` with a single-stream QKV entry point, prepare real rotary tables once after sequence sharding, and preserve the existing native/CUDA fallback. Remove the separate adapter files and vendor-specific model settings from the earlier revision. Keep this revision eager-only.

### 4. Whose customer or user needs does this address, and what are those needs?

Ascend users running Qwen-Image-2.1 who need the fused preprocessing integration to fit the existing model, prefix cache, and parallel attention paths. The implementation and acceptance scope originate in the author's [#8774](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8774); this revision expands the metadata-based eligibility checks while retaining eager-only execution.

## Purpose

Before this change, Qwen-Image-2.1 uses the existing Q/K norm and rotary paths, including native NPU RoPE. This revision first tries the public `mindiesd.norm_rope_concat` API for eligible eager NPU inputs; otherwise it retains the existing `qk_rotary` or RMSNorm + rotary chain.

- Reuse the existing shared layer for single-stream `[B, S, N, D]` Q/K/V. Pass `input_layout="BSND"` and `output_layout="BSND"` explicitly. Outputs are logical BSND and may be noncontiguous; physically contiguous BSND is not required.
- Interpret Qwen complex frequencies in the model. Prepare `norm_rope_concat_tables` through `prepare_norm_rope_concat_tables` once per eligible eager forward after SP sharding/padding; these expanded `(cos, sin)` tables are specific to that operator. CUDA fusion and independent rotary paths consume the existing complex `freqs` directly.
- Encapsulate norm eligibility and the two fusion attempts in a private attention method returning Q/K/V or `None`. QK-only fusion retains the original V; the forward loop has one independent Norm/RoPE fallback.
- Apply fusion only to fresh projected tokens, before prefix-cache storage/quantization. Preserve CFG branch ownership, FP8/FP8-V cache handling, SP joint tensors, masking, and attention selection.
- Do not gate fusion on A5, batch1, TP1/SP1, or native-cache configuration. Check actual tensor geometry, dtype/device, weights, tables, and public API availability. This removes configuration restrictions; it does **not** establish runtime support for every combination.
- Retain `enforce_eager=True` as a model-level prerequisite. Compilation tracing returns to the existing path. No SD Fake/Meta or NPU graph support is added.
- Resolve the public API lazily on first use and cache it for the process; importing the shared layer does not initialize an operator callable. Use operator-specific capability and input-validation names; hardware checks stay in the shared layer.
- Propagate execution errors after selecting the operator. Missing or unsupported public API/input contracts fall back.
- Add coverage to the existing shared-layer and Qwen numerical tests, select the shared NPU tests in the A2/A3/A5 Ready lanes, and add portable real-model T2I/I2I tests to CUDA Ready/Merge and NPU Ready.

Compared with the earlier PR revision, `fused_norm_rope.py`, `qwen_image_21/qkv_norm_rope.py`, the two vendor/layout settings, the head-major prefix-concat helper, and the added feature documentation/recipe edits are absent. Prefix K/V concatenation follows main.

The [attention selection](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/668d517fa8b69b86400a120179d7a1d9130a0bf0/docs/design/feature/attention_backend_selection.md), [SP](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/668d517fa8b69b86400a120179d7a1d9130a0bf0/docs/design/feature/sequence_parallel.md), and [TP](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/668d517fa8b69b86400a120179d7a1d9130a0bf0/docs/design/feature/tensor_parallel.md) contracts remain unchanged. No new public configuration option or example is introduced, so their documentation is unchanged.

Related: #8774, RFC #8586. The current candidate has completed real A5 functional, image-observation and profiling runs. It has not established an overall E2E speedup; image-quality acceptance and a consumable MindIE-SD dependency release remain pending.

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** `0.32.0+empty`; `vllm-ascend 0.19.1rc2.dev2959+g450e55698.d20261020`, PyTorch `2.10.0+cpu`, `torch-npu 2.10.0.post4`, Python 3.12.13.

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** `d4d01231635e3ca8504a6cedfc1d37557b7dd335`, based on main `95b1d97f2ec2dc1d93a3e9743bf962b2faaad47b`. Original commits and subsequent review fixes are preserved; squash is deferred.

Real tests use Ascend950PR (A5) and the frozen `nightly-20261021-24f0cf3-a5` image. The image's MindIE-SD 3.1.0 package was overlaid privately with the public layout wrapper and compiled OPP from SD `e8f079db64876d000855ed9832b17fc2e2f77ceb`. No installed shared package was overwritten and no Fake/Meta implementation was added. **The image's unmodified MindIE-SD package alone does not supply this public layout API.** A consumable dependency release remains pending.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/diffusion/layers/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_npu.py \
  tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_transformer_numerics.py \
  -k 'single_stream or qkv_' -m 'cpu or A5' --run-level core_model

python -m pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/offline_inference/test_qwen_image_21.py \
  -m 'core_model and npu and A5 and cards_1' --run-level core_model
```

Missing public MindIE-SD API is skipped by hardware tests; a skip is not kernel validation.

## Test Result

- **45 passed, 19 deselected** in the real installed-vLLM environment: 41 CPU contract cases and four actual A5 numerical cases. These execute packed noncontiguous projection views, compare Q/K against FP32 composition, verify V exactly, and assert compilation returns `None`.
- **2 passed** for the checked-in portable T2I/I2I E2E tests with real model weights (512x512, four steps, seed 42, CFG1).
- **TP=2 and Ulysses SP=2** each completed real T2I and I2I requests with two workers. Each configuration recorded 640 public fused calls across engine startup warmup and the two requests, including prefill/decode token shapes. TP used 16 local heads; SP used 32 heads and 512 local target tokens. These functional checks are not performance measurements.
- Real attention-level fused/unfused comparisons passed for native, FP8 K/V and FP8-V prefix caches, batch=2, both CFG branches, prefill and two decode iterations: 18 fused calls, `atol=rtol=0.04`.
- Twelve additional real-A5 cases passed across FP16/BF16/FP32, interleaved/half-split rotation and contiguous/packed inputs; V remained exact. A full real-model FP8 K/V cache T2I/I2I run passed with actual float8 cache storage and 320 fused calls including warmup. Full `enforce_eager=False` requests passed with the observer enabled and zero SD fused calls.
- Changed-file Ruff, formatting, SPDX, test marks, forbidden-import/device-call policy, mypy-3.10, Buildkite schema and diff checks passed. Public [pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/actions/runs/39645360332) [wheel build](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/actions/runs/39645360498), and [CodeQL](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/actions/runs/39645360445) passed for this head.
- An independent review using the repository's `review-pr` skill found one stale compile-success test assertion; it was corrected and re-reviewed. No remaining P1/P2 finding was reported. Human review is not marked complete.
- **124 requests completed with exit 0** in the fixed-main A/B batch: 20 pure E2E samples, 20 separate component-timing samples, four profiling requests, 24 preserved warmups and 56 visual-observation images. Both scenes use BF16/eager/native cache/TP1/SP1, 1024x1024, 50 steps and CFG1; timing uses seed 42 and alternates AB/BA. The 56 images cover 14 cases and seeds 0/42. All original image hashes and eight complete prefill/decode traces/kernel tables were verified.
- Each of the eight single-Transformer profile windows contains 32 attention calls. Candidate windows contain 32 actual NormRopeConcat kernels; baseline windows contain zero. Prefill/decode were distinguished by the real prefix-cache state, at forward indices 0/10. Kernel-duration sums are not treated as E2E timings.
- The first timing batch reached 50–93°C and had varying actual clocks. Its median baseline/candidate E2E ratios were 0.9943x (T2I) and 0.9880x (I2I); those observations do not establish a stable speedup or regression.
- An additional **28-request E2E-only repeat completed with exit 0**, waiting for a temperature reading <=67°C before every request. Each scene/arm used two warmups and five pure timing samples; cooldown time was excluded. T2I medians were **12.941752s baseline / 12.905783s candidate (1.002787x)**; I2I medians were **15.628137s / 15.752516s (0.992104x)**. Runtime clocks still varied. **These results do not establish an overall E2E performance improvement.** Cold-batch E2E values are not combined with the earlier hot-batch component columns.
- Visual inspection found broadly similar composition and editing behavior with local detail/text changes. Both arms have incorrect Chinese stage labels/small text in the AI-timeline case, and some characters/numbers differ. This is an observation, **not image-quality equivalence or human acceptance**.
- A runtime-only native-prefix-cache contiguous-clone experiment reduced decode Cat_Transpose counts from 128 to 64, with identical pixels across 20 requests, but only about 1.000968x median E2E and overlapping ranges. **That cache-layout change was not adopted into this PR.**
- CUDA/A2/A3 runtime combinations, SP padding on real devices and downstream hardware CI remain unverified. No graph-support claim is made; non-eager full-model requests validate fallback only.
- SD fuses normalization/affine/rotation before its final cast, whereas the main fallback can round between operations. Bitwise equivalence and image-quality acceptance are not claimed. Earlier revisions' timing/image results do not validate this tree.

issues.title: [Kernel] Fuse Qwen-Image 2.1 blocks with SM90-correct rounding
issues.body:
The Qwen-Image 2.1 eager block spends many launches on Q/K normalization and complex RoPE, SwiGLU, modulation and gated residuals. This PR fuses those pointwise chains while preserving BF16 rounding, now directly based on main. The previous offload-residency change is preserved separately and excluded from this fusion PR.

The H100 update matches ATen's imaginary complex-product FMA order on SM90. It also addresses the two existing review findings: singleton modulation rows are rejected when the selected mode requires more rows, and ineligible sublayers use the eager residual path.

Related to #8586 **A1**. The measured configuration is a **B3 four-independent-replica workload**; this result does not complete the TP/CFG/SP topology comparison.

### H100 fusion-only result

Pinned baseline `3dc35694`, measured fusion source `287d9483`, and `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1@b3179ad355be050328e483a9dfdd9e60cd62adfa`. Four exclusive H100s, four TP1/SP1/CFG1 servers, actual DiT B1, HTTP C64, BF16, 1024x1024, 50 steps, eager, FLASH_ATTN, no offload or decode graph. Each fresh start has 4 initial, 8 warmup and 16 qualification requests outside timing, then 128 measured requests.

| Round | Baseline images/s | Fusion images/s | Baseline P95 s | Fusion P95 s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.427811 | 0.618699 | 149.579 | 103.159 |
| 2 | 0.427446 | 0.618552 | 149.690 | 103.194 |

A/B/B/A mean throughput: **0.427628 -> 0.618625 images/s (+44.66%)**; mean P95 **-31.05%**. All **256 paired timed images have identical decoded RGB pixels**. Sampled maximum single-device NVML memory: 33.506 -> 33.494 GiB; one-second samples may miss transient peaks. All four trials had no foreign GPU processes.

PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM 0.31.0, Transformers 5.14.1, Diffusers 0.40.0, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1; NVIDIA driver 595.91.07. Devices report 65,247 MiB each. These are two paired rounds at one fixed load, rather than a broad scaling claim.

[Full configuration, measurements and exact reproduction commands](https://github.com/0z5a/vllm-omni/blob/6407c92258f9df4e26df5dfa887295dd27387f17/docs/performance/qwen_image_21_fusion_h100.md). The checked-in [HTTP replica benchmark](https://github.com/0z5a/vllm-omni/blob/6407c92258f9df4e26df5dfa887295dd27387f17/benchmarks/diffusion/benchmark_image_replicas.py) records request-level latency, failures and decoded-image hashes.

### Validation and limits

- Recorded H100 fusion suite: **59 passed** across `test_fused_kernels.py`, `test_modulation_fusion.py` and `test_gated_norm_fusion.py`.
- Current submission checks: all applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, mypy, marks and import/device checks.
- Current CPU host-function isolation: **12 contract probes pass** for strict row rejection and valid B1 eager outputs. This does not exercise package import or CUDA.
- The benchmark's local real-HTTP fixture passes 128 simultaneous requests while retaining two intentional failures; duration-based issuing and drain also pass.
- Four new CUDA fallback regressions for strided/FP32 sublayers are added but **have not run on this macOS host**. The H100 performance table belongs to the pinned measured source above, before these extra unsupported-input guards. The normal contiguous BF16 GPU kernels are unchanged.
- Earlier shared-node H100 speed measurements were affected by another experiment; the exclusive four-trial result supersedes them.
- The original combined offload implementation is preserved at [the legacy source](https://github.com/0z5a/vllm-omni/tree/abd3d8c2d4faa59c5f44c16672cfbbb535b8c73a); its A100 results are excluded from this fusion PR. Generated images are model outputs, not ground truth.

issues.title: [Perf][Qwen-Image-2.1] Drop dead VAE feature-cache clones for single-frame images
issues.body:
## Purpose

Part of #8586 (C2). Related: #8099.

CUDA A/B of the VAE alone (bf16; H100, RTX 5090, RTX 4090) is in **Test Result**: the 1024² decode peak drops by 2.90 GiB, untiled 2048² decode goes from OOM to running on the 24 GB and 32 GB cards, and outputs are `torch.equal`. End to end on H100 at 1024², the whole-request peak allocated drops from 36.86 to 33.96 GiB (−2.90 GiB, matching luca-888's estimate below) with identical images, and layerwise offload at 1024² on an RTX 4090 goes from OOM in VAE decode to running; at 2048² the offload configs on 24/32 GB cards still need VAE tiling.

### Mechanism

Line numbers are on `36082d2ec`. These files have not changed since #8099.

- `QwenImage21CausalConv3d` (`vllm_omni/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/autoencoder_kl_qwenimage21.py:164`) subclasses `nn.Conv2d`, and its `forward` asserts `cache_x is None` (`:201`). The Wan-style temporal feature cache is therefore never read.
- Encode and decode still pass `self._feat_map` / `self._enc_feat_map`, so every cached conv clones its input first: `cache_x = x[:, :, -CACHE_T:, :, :].clone()` at `:388/:407/:625/:650/:914/:936`. The encoder's temporal downsample also stores `x.clone()` at `:337`. With one frame, `x[:, :, -2:]` is the whole activation.
- The clones stay in the map until `clear_cache()` runs after the call:
  - `_decode`: `:1342-1361`
  - `_encode`: `:1280-1304`
  - per tile in `tiled_decode` (`:1570-1582`) and `tiled_encode` (`:1443-1463`)
  - `tile_exec`: `vllm_omni/diffusion/distributed/autoencoders/autoencoder_kl_qwenimage21.py:89-100`
- Untiled decode is the default (`vae_use_tiling=False`).

### Change

The encoder and decoder are now called without a feature cache at all 5 call sites: `_encode`, `_decode`, `tiled_encode`, `tiled_decode` and `tile_exec`. `first_chunk` is unchanged. The per-frame `_conv_idx` / `_enc_conv_idx` resets are gone, since they only served the cache walk.

For one frame, the cached and uncached walks run the same ops, so the output does not change:
- every conv gets `cache_x=None`;
- the first-chunk `upsample3d` stores `"Rep"` and skips `time_conv`;
- the first-chunk `downsample3d` stores a clone and skips `time_conv`.

### Intentionally kept

- `clear_cache()`, its call sites and the `try/finally` blocks. The existing OOM-cleanup tests and `tile_merge` use them.
- The `if feat_cache is not None` branches inside the submodules. They keep the Wan-derived diffusers structure, and the new test uses them as the cached reference. Removing them would be a separate cleanup of about 100 lines, if reviewers prefer.
- `x_copy = x.clone()` at `:532/:731`. That is a separate question and has not been checked.
- Multi-frame input stays unsupported. The only change is one error type:

  | Input | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | decode T=2 | fails in `post_quant_conv` | same |
  | encode T=2 | returns one latent frame (1+4k chunking) | same |
  | encode T=5 | `AssertionError` at `:201` | conv2d 5-D `RuntimeError` |

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.31.0.
- CPU tests: vLLM source on `PYTHONPATH`, torch 2.13.0 (CPU), diffusers 0.40.0, Python 3.12, Apple M5 Pro.
- CUDA A/B: vLLM 0.31.0 wheel with torch 2.13.0+cu130, diffusers 0.40.0, on RunPod H100 80GB HBM3, RTX 5090 32GB and RTX 4090 24GB (one GPU each).

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** base `36082d2ec`, this branch `d8ea5d198`. The CUDA A/B ran on the C2 pin `3dc35694` (#8099) with and without this change; the two VAE files there are byte-identical to `36082d2ec` and to this branch respectively.

New tests are in `tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_vae.py`. They run on CPU with a toy VAE that has one temporal stage, so the `downsample3d`, `upsample3d` and `first_chunk` branches all run. Both are parametrized over decode, tiled_decode, tile_exec, encode and tiled_encode:

- `test_single_frame_paths_hold_no_feature_cache`: the encoder and decoder never receive a feature cache, and no cached tensor is left in `_feat_map` or `_enc_feat_map`. It fails on the base commit (5/5) and passes here.
- `test_single_frame_paths_match_cached_reference`: the output is deterministic, and it is `torch.equal` to a reference run that gives every encoder/decoder call a fresh cache, the way the old call sites did. It also passes on the base commit, which checks the reference itself.

```bash
pytest -q tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_vae.py
pytest -q tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21 \
  tests/diffusion/distributed/test_distributed_vae_executor.py \
  tests/diffusion/distributed/test_vae_error_recovery.py \
  tests/diffusion/distributed/test_vae_batch_parallel.py
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm_omni/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/autoencoder_kl_qwenimage21.py \
  vllm_omni/diffusion/distributed/autoencoders/autoencoder_kl_qwenimage21.py \
  tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_vae.py
```

CPU probe (a scratch script, not checked in; I can attach it):
- It uses the `vae/config.json` from HF `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1@d26bb612` with random weights.
- It loads the base-commit module file next to the patched one, with the same state_dict, and compares outputs with `torch.equal`.
- It counts the cached tensors that are still alive when the encoder/decoder forward returns.

CUDA A/B (VAE only, part of the #8586 C2 run):
- Loads only `vae/` of `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1@d26bb612` in bf16 on one GPU; base and fix use the same weights and the same seeded latents/images.
- Per op: 1 warm-up + 3 timed runs, `torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()` before each; peak = `max_memory_allocated` / `max_memory_reserved` during the op; transient = peak allocated minus allocated before the op.
- Outputs of base and fix are compared with `torch.equal`.
- End to end: C2 matrix cells (`Omni(...)`, T2I, 50 steps, seed 42, bf16), each run once with the pinned code and once with this change on the same pod and spec; peak allocated from in-process memory probes (`max_memory_allocated`, reset at each stage boundary); peak reserved = vllm-omni's own `peak_memory_mb` from the passive feasibility run; latency = mean of the measured runs with the probe off.

## Test Result

```text
test_vae.py:  19 passed
broader set:  117 passed, 8 failed
```

The 8 failures are the same on the base commit, and they all need CUDA (`Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled`): 4 in `test_decode_graph.py` and 4 in `test_transformer_numerics.py`.

All pre-commit hooks that apply to the changed files pass: ruff check/format 0.14.10, typos, mypy-3.10, check-mark, SPDX, forbidden imports and torch.cuda.

**Bit-identical output** (CPU, real 2.1 VAE config, random weights; `torch.equal`, max abs diff 0):

| Path | fp32 128 px | fp32 256 px | bf16 64 px |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode | yes | yes | yes |
| tiled_decode (3×3 tiles; 2×2 at 64 px) | yes | yes | yes |
| encode | yes | yes | yes |
| tiled_encode (3×3 tiles; 2×2 at 64 px) | yes | yes | yes |
| tile_exec | covered only by the toy-config unit test | | |

**Feature-cache tensors still alive when the encoder/decoder returns** (bf16, batch 1, one frame, untiled):

| Resolution | Decoder before | Decoder after | Encoder before | Encoder after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024² | 36 tensors, 4.03 GiB | 0 | 29 tensors, 1.43 GiB | 0 |
| 1536² | 36 tensors, 9.06 GiB | 0 | 29 tensors, 3.21 GiB | 0 |
| 2048² | 36 tensors, 16.10 GiB | 0 | 29 tensors, 5.70 GiB | 0 |

- The 1024²–2048² rows are computed from tensor shapes on the meta device, with no compute.
- The same counter on real CPU runs at 128² and 256² gives the same 36 and 29 tensors and the same 2061.2 decoder elements per output pixel.
- Tiled decode holds one tile's worth at a time, about 1.0 GiB for the default 512² tile (extrapolated, not measured).

These numbers are the clones alive at the end of the decoder. They are an upper bound on the peak reduction, not a measured peak; the measured peaks are below.

**CUDA, VAE only** (bf16, batch 1; GiB; latency = median of 3 timed runs):

| Op | GPU | Before: peak alloc / reserved | After: peak alloc / reserved | Δ alloc | Latency before → after | `torch.equal` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode 1024² | H100 | 7.20 / 8.48 | 4.30 / 6.47 | −2.90 | 126.3 → 124.6 ms | yes |
| decode 1536² | H100 | 15.40 / 17.72 | 8.87 / 13.38 | −6.52 | 279.7 → 267.9 ms | yes |
| decode 2048² | H100 | 26.87 / 33.23 | 15.28 / 23.38 | −11.59 | 486.9 → 471.7 ms | yes |
| decode 2048² | RTX 5090 32GB | OOM | 15.28 / 23.36 | | – → 777.5 ms | – |
| decode 2048² | RTX 4090 24GB | OOM | 15.28 / 20.00 | | – → 1332.1 ms | – |
| decode 2048², tiled | H100 | 2.33 / 2.62 | 1.61 / 2.20 | −0.73 | 1139.3 → 1115.1 ms | yes |
| encode 1024² | H100 | 2.90 / 3.15 | 2.15 / 2.57 | −0.76 | 35.9 → 33.6 ms | yes |

- RTX 5090 and RTX 4090 give the same allocated peaks as H100 at 1024² and 1536² (within 0.01 GiB), and `torch.equal` holds there too.
- Before the change, the 1024² decode transient is 6.56 GiB, the same as the VAE decode transient in A0; after, 3.66 GiB.
- The OOM rows are the VAE alone on an otherwise empty GPU; whether a full pipeline fits depends on the offload config, which the end-to-end cells cover.

**CUDA, end-to-end T2I** (GiB, peak allocated / peak reserved; same GPU and spec before/after):

| Config, resolution | GPU | Before | After | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E0 (eager, no offload), 1024² | H100 | 36.86 / 38.12 | 33.96 / 36.53 (−2.90 / −1.59) | images identical (max abs diff 0) |
| D0 (default: compile + CUDA-graph decode), 1024² | H100 | 37.00 / 38.84 | 34.10 / 36.73 (−2.90 / −2.11) | images identical (max abs diff 0) |
| LW (layerwise offload), 1024² | RTX 4090 24GB | OOM in VAE decode | – / 22.78, 27.35 s/img | |
| ME (model offload), 2048² | RTX 5090 32GB / RTX 4090 24GB | OOM in VAE decode | OOM in VAE decode | |
| LW (layerwise offload), 2048² | RTX 5090 32GB / RTX 4090 24GB | OOM in VAE decode (5090); not run on 4090, since 1024² already OOM | OOM in VAE decode | |

- Before the change, E0 matches A0: peak allocated 36.86 GiB, resident after the request 30.30 (A0: 30.29), decode transient 6.56, peak reserved 38.12. After: decode transient 3.66 GiB, and the VAE feature cache held at the peak goes from 3.75 GiB to 0; the diffusion-stage peak is unchanged (30.87).
- Latency is unchanged within run-to-run noise (probe off: E0 7.84 → 7.59 s/img, D0 5.84 → 5.82 s/img).
- At 2048² the remaining decode activations are still too large for these cards untiled; the tiled configs (MET, LWT) already fit for T2I at 2048² on both cards (base runs).
- The OOM stage comes from the tracebacks (`interpolate` / `normalize` inside the VAE decoder).
- The allocated peaks come from a second H100 run with per-stage memory probes (in the first run the probe recorded nothing, a bug in my measurement harness, not in vllm-omni); the reserved peaks of the two runs agree within 0.01 GiB.

**End-to-end image edit (luca-888's run, not mine).** On H200 at 1024², luca-888 measured the whole-request peak allocated for image edit going from 36.87 to 33.97 GiB (−2.90 GiB) with identical outputs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6163716714. The "before" value matches my H100 E0 edit cell (36.87 GiB); I have not run the edit "after" cell myself.

luca-888 checked this against the A0 memory snapshots (H200, 1024², bf16) in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6076184808:
- At the peak, 3.74 GiB of the 6.56 GiB VAE decode transient are these clones.
- Dropping them should take the whole-request peak from 36.86 GiB to about 33.96 GiB, roughly 2.9 GiB.
- Measured: the whole-request peak goes from 36.86 to 33.96 GiB (E0, 1024²), and the VAE-only decode peak drops by 2.90 GiB.

**Not verified yet:**
- The multi-GPU distributed VAE path. Only the toy-config `tile_exec` hooks were run, on CPU.

## Purpose

Continues / supersedes #7759 for release landing.

issues.title: [Perf] Dequantize the FP8 prefix K/V straight into the packed buffer for Qwen-Image 2.1
issues.body:
## Purpose

Fuse FP8 prefix K/V dequantization and packing for Qwen-Image 2.1. Instead of materializing a BF16 prefix and concatenating it with the target K/V, one Triton kernel writes both directly into the packed buffer. This removes the intermediate allocation and reduces dequantize/pack launches from 8 to 2 for K+V FP8.

The cache format, BF16 rounding and attention computation stay unchanged. Native-dtype prefixes keep `torch.cat`; the fusion supports strided K/V views and adds no persistent buffers. Quantized-cache decode remains eager, and the Ulysses SP path is unchanged.

[Incremental diff against the prerequisite](https://github.com/0z5a/vllm-omni/compare/d9bb1c9158a6e5769f7c742e305d1796e07b9272...2158688bde21282c0d4cc7dba6c80cd2f3212d47).

## Test Plan

**A100 40GB, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM 0.30.0.** Baseline `d9bb1c9158a6`, PR `2158688bde21`. Full `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` checkpoint at `b3179ad355be`, image editing with a 1024×1024 reference, 512×512 output, 40 steps, CFG=1, BF16 attention and FP8 E4M3 prefix K/V (~4,126 tokens).

One fresh process per arm and configuration, 2 serial + 64 concurrent warmup requests, then one burst of C requests at each concurrency. Timing is unprofiled. B1 uses FlashAttention; configured B2 uses SDPA. Each row compares the same backend and configuration.

## Test Result

**19 native regression tests passed**, including strided V, fallback paths and all 256 E4M3 byte encodings. Across both configurations, **480/480 measured requests completed**; all **240 measured image pairs and 132 warmup pairs matched pixel-for-pixel**. All four processes exited naturally.

| Configuration | Concurrency | Baseline img/s | PR img/s | Throughput gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B1 / FlashAttention | 8 | 0.1552 | 0.1765 | +13.75% |
| B1 / FlashAttention | 16 | 0.1549 | 0.1763 | +13.81% |
| B1 / FlashAttention | 32 | 0.1547 | 0.1761 | +13.79% |
| B1 / FlashAttention | 64 | 0.1548 | 0.1761 | +13.79% |
| Configured B2 / SDPA | 8 | 0.1426 | 0.1598 | +12.05% |
| Configured B2 / SDPA | 16 | 0.1409 | 0.1574 | +11.76% |
| Configured B2 / SDPA | 32 | 0.1399 | 0.1569 | +12.16% |
| Configured B2 / SDPA | 64 | 0.1395 | 0.1563 | +12.01% |

Configured B2 executes mixed B1/B2 steps: both arms recorded 80 B1 steps per cell and 120/280/600/1,240 B2 steps at C8/16/32/64. These are within-configuration gains, not a comparison of batch scaling. B1 peak allocated memory was 32.33 GiB in both arms.

These are exploratory single-start pairs. Background CPU preparation overlapped the B1 baseline; a file transfer may overlap the start of B2/C8. Repeated starts and a fresh B2/C8 comparison remain pending. The table covers long-prefix image editing; it does not establish a gain for short-prefix text-to-image or V-only FP8.

issues.title: [Kernel] Fuse Q/K RMSNorm+RoPE and the SwiGLU activation for Qwen-Image 2.1
issues.body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/7944/files) against `qwen-image-2.1`.

## Scope

Fuses two pointwise regions of the Qwen-Image-2.1 single-stream DiT block. Both are pure
elementwise work that the eager block spreads over many kernels and temporary tensors.

**Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE** (`QwenImage21Attention.forward`). The eager block splits the packed
`to_qkv` projection, normalizes Q and K, and then rotates them with an interleaved
complex-pair RoPE. That is ten kernels per block per step over two full head stacks
(FP32 reduction, rounding cast, learned scale, FP32 promotion, complex multiply, output
cast). One Triton launch now covers the whole chain over the packed Q-then-K head region.
V is untouched, the QKV GEMM is untouched, and nothing is written in place.

**SwiGLU activation** (`QwenImage21SwiGLUFeedForward`). `silu(gate) * up` becomes one
two-input kernel. The two `ColumnParallelLinear` projections and the checkpoint names are
unchanged; this deliberately does **not** adopt vLLM's packed `SiluAndMul`, because that
would need a per-forward `torch.cat([gate, up])` whose copy costs more than the activation
kernel it replaces.

Out of scope: the QKV/down GEMMs, weight repacking, merged gate/up projections, attention
masks and collectives.

## Baseline

| item | value |
|---|---|
| base branch | `qwen-image-2.1` |
| base SHA | `3ea9e605011fc2a0bfa9f3e8531286fb683068dd` (#7759 head) |
| GPU | RTX 5090 (SM120), 32 GB |
| dtype | bfloat16, eager and CUDA-graph decode |
| torch / triton / vLLM | 2.13.0+cu130 / 3.7.1 / 0.29.0 |

## Numerical and execution contract

The fused kernels reproduce the eager rounding points exactly rather than folding them:

```
var  = fp32 mean of x^2 over the head dim       # fp32 reduction
unit = (x * rsqrt(var + eps)).to(bfloat16)      # round BEFORE the learned scale
norm = unit * weight                            # bfloat16 x bfloat16
out  = fma(a, c, -(b * d)), fma(b, c, a * d)    # ATen's complex64 multiply association
```

Two details matter and are the reason this cannot reuse `layers/fused_qk_norm_rope.py`:

* the upstream zero-tolerance test pins the round-to-BF16 *between* the normalization and the
  learned scale, so the kernel reproduces that rounding point explicitly;
* Qwen-Image-2.1 RoPE is the **interleaved complex-pair** layout, not rotate-half, and its
  frequency table is `complex64`.

For the SwiGLU, ATen's `silu` on a BF16 tensor promotes to FP32, computes `x / (1 + expf(-x))`
and rounds back — it divides, it does not multiply by a sigmoid, and `tl.exp`/`tl.sigmoid`
lower to different hardware instructions than ATen's libdevice calls.

`vllm_omni/diffusion/layers/numerics.py` holds the pinned-rounding primitives that make this
reproducible (`round_bf16_to_fp32`, `add/mul/sub/fma_rn_f32`, `rsqrt_approx_f32`,
`div_rn_f32`, `exp_f32`, `silu_f32`). LTX-2's `ops/_numerics.py` now re-exports the same
module instead of keeping a second copy; the LTX-2 op modules and unit tests are unchanged
and still pass.

Eligibility is explicit and everything else falls back to the eager chain: CUDA + Triton,
BF16, 4-D with a unit last stride, power-of-two head dim, `2 * freqs.shape[-1] == head_dim`,
matching norm-weight shapes, and contiguous equal-shaped gate/up. FP16, CPU and non-contiguous
layouts take the original path and are covered by tests.

## Validation

Bit-exactness, `torch.equal` against the eager chain (no tolerance):

| region | shapes covered | mismatches |
|---|---|---|
| Q/K norm + RoPE | B ∈ {1,2}, S ∈ {1,17,256,4096} | **0 / 107,397,120** |
| SwiGLU | B ∈ {1,2}, S ∈ {1,256,300,4096}, hidden ∈ {3072,12288}; tails 1/7/4095/4096/4097/100000 | **0 / 69,453,480** |

Tests added in `tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_fused_kernels.py`:
op-level equality on CPU and CUDA, strided packed-QKV views, the real
`QwenImage21Attention.forward` and `QwenImage21SwiGLUFeedForward.forward` against an
eager-replacement monkeypatch, V-untouched and output-ownership checks, and the FP16 /
non-contiguous / short-head-dim fallbacks.

`tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/` passes in full (113 tests including the untouched
upstream numerical tests), and the LTX-2 op/transformer/attention tests pass (38 passed,
2 skipped) with the shared `_numerics` module.

## Performance

### Operator microbenchmark (RTX 5090, real layout, CUDA events, warmed)

`kernel` = sum of device kernel time per call; `op` = full op path including the wrapper and
its allocation. `kernels` counts device kernels per call.

**Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE** (`heads=32, head_dim=128`)

| B | S | op eager µs | op fused µs | speedup | kernel eager µs | kernel fused µs | kernels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 256 | 214.6 | 36.9 | 5.81x | 52.3 | 4.7 | 10 → 1 |
| 1 | 4096 | 783.8 | 78.2 | 10.02x | 753.9 | 75.7 | 10 → 1 |
| 1 | 4608 | 1022.6 | 99.7 | 10.26x | 997.1 | 97.0 | 10 → 1 |
| 2 | 4096 | 2307.5 | 177.9 | 12.97x | 2280.5 | 175.1 | 10 → 1 |

**SwiGLU** (`hidden=4096`, so the MLP hidden width is 12288)

| B | S | op eager µs | op fused µs | speedup | kernel eager µs | kernel fused µs | kernels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 256 | 24.9 | 24.4 | 1.02x | 6.5 | 6.0 | 2 → 1 |
| 1 | 4608 | 363.6 | 216.0 | 1.68x | 360.3 | 213.8 | 2 → 1 |
| 2 | 4096 | 646.9 | 384.0 | 1.68x | 642.9 | 382.0 | 2 → 1 |

Each row is the median of five independent CUDA-event timing rounds. The SwiGLU kernel itself
Repeated full benchmark runs varied by a few percent on this shared host (e.g. the S=4608 Q/K row measured 10.17x-10.26x across runs, the A4 `K+V` P=4608 row 4.40x-4.56x); the tables above are one representative run each and all of them are within that spread.
is faster at every size; at S=256 the op path is a wash (1.02x) because the custom-op dispatch
and the output allocation are larger than the kernel time. Under CUDA-graph decode that host
cost is amortised away, so the kernel-time reduction is the number that carries.

### Model-level integration check (weights-free)

The real `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel` was built from a small config (3 layers, 4 heads,
head_dim 128, inner 512, `axes_dims_rope` kept at the published `(16, 56, 56)`) with
deterministically initialised random weights — every parameter overwritten as
`randn(sha256(name) ^ seed) * 0.05` so a renamed or reshaped parameter would show up as a
mismatch — and the real `Attention` layer on `SDPABackend`. Two realistic token layouts
(condition-image blocks + target image block + text, so the `t = 0` modulation row,
`target_token_mask`, the block-causal mask and the key-padding hole are all exercised) were
run through both a full forward and a prefill → target-only KV-cache decode, under four KV
configurations (`native`, `fp8`, `fp8_v`, `causal_condition=False`).

Result: `torch.equal` is `True` and `max |a - b| == 0.0` on every dumped tensor (37 forward,
23 decode per configuration) for every configuration. Patch activity was confirmed by kernel
name rather than assumed: `_qk_norm_rope_kernel` and `_silu_mul_kernel` (3 per layer) launch in
both the prefill and the decode of all 8 configurations, and the baseline launches neither.

This is an integration and rounding check on randomly initialised weights, not a
checkpoint-quality or image-quality validation.

### Complete request — T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps, cfg=1.0, seed=42

| metric | baseline median | patch median | speedup | latency reduction | per-round pairs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `wall_ms` | 15156.48 | 14227.18 | **1.065x** (geo 1.068x) | 6.13% | 15196.7/14227.2, 15151.0/14233.0, 15156.5/14166.0 |
| `phase_ms.denoise` | 14723.91 | 13769.71 | **1.069x** (geo 1.070x) | 6.48% | 14736.0/13787.9, 14714.4/13769.7, 14723.9/13744.0 |
| `denoise_ms_per_step` | 368.10 | 344.24 | **1.069x** (geo 1.070x) | 6.48% | 368.4/344.7, 367.9/344.2, 368.1/343.6 |

Baseline and patch run the same fixed workload from independent source checkouts in fresh processes, 3 measured rounds plus 1 warmup, with the within-round order flipped every round. Speedup is `baseline / patch`; latency reduction is `(baseline - patch) / baseline`.

Output image sha256 — baseline `93876c8820fc086b9e0c3fe8f467fa953ce770bf9fadc377e36ed7f63281705d`, patch `93876c8820fc086b9e0c3fe8f467fa953ce770bf9fadc377e36ed7f63281705d`. Bit-identical: **True**. Failed runs: 0.

**Measurement note.** Both arms run the same `--layerwise-offload` configuration. The 33.1 GB
checkpoint does not fit on one 32 GB card — plain and `--cpu-offload` both OOM during the engine's
startup warmup — so layerwise weight streaming sits in the critical path and dilutes the
kernel-level gain. The operator microbenchmark above is the offload-free measurement; this table
is the complete-request number in the only configuration that runs on this hardware.

## Not validated

* FP16 and FP32 DiT weights (explicit fallback; not measured).
* TP > 1 and Ulysses SP end-to-end (the kernel handles rank-local head counts; the fused op
  has not been run on a multi-rank topology).
* LoRA adapters on the fused projections.
* Quantized (FP8/INT8/NVFP4) linear layers feeding the fused ops.
